verdict.justification: Both reports correctly identify A-300-K02 as the assigned location for P11-P09457-01, preserve the three logged receipt quantities, and flag that the supplied files cannot support a fully quantified put-away report. A is more useful operationally because its missing-quantity row contains guarded formulas that populate when the receipt quantity is confirmed, whereas B leaves text placeholders such as "TBD (= half of qty rec'd)" requiring manual replacement. A also provides a clear reconciliation total for logged receipts and a separate cross-reference showing source quantities, supplier back-orders, and location-match results. Both adopt the questionable interpretation that half of the received quantity was moved, but A explicitly flags that ambiguity and provides the alternative treatment, "set F3 = C3 (Balance 0)," if the instruction means a half shipment was received and entirely moved. B does not offer that qualification and includes irrelevant process commentary about empty workspace folders. Although A is more verbose, its stronger audit trail and actionable exception handling make it the preferable workbook.

decisive_issues.issue: The key movement quantity is a text placeholder rather than a formula ready to calculate after confirmation.
Explicitly acknowledges the ambiguous half-shipment instruction and gives the alternative accounting treatment.
decisive_issues.quote: If it instead means the delivery was a half shipment and all of it was moved, set F3 = C3 (Balance 0).

decisive_issues.issue: Includes a scoped reconciliation total that excludes the unquantified receipt.
Includes internal workspace commentary unrelated to the inventory report.
